cards.explanation: The answer is that they carry it out. Micah says it plainly: “At morning’s light they accomplish it because the power is in their hands.” The plan made on the bed gets carried out when the light comes. That's what Micah's woe is aimed at, friends.

The answer is covet. Micah 2:2 says, “They covet fields and seize them; they take away houses.” Coveting and seizing show up in the same line, friends. Verse 1 already told us the power is in their hands.

The answer is a disaster they cannot escape. The LORD says, “I am planning against this nation a disaster from which you cannot free your necks.” Picture a collar you can't wriggle out of, friends. These schemers spent the night planning, and now the LORD declares His own plan.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Then you will not walk so proudly, for it will be a time of calamity.” Just before that, He speaks of “…a disaster from which you cannot free your necks.” That's the LORD's word on how they will walk, friends.

The answer is that it has been removed. The lament says, “He has changed the portion of my people. How He has removed it from me!” The speakers say the portion has been removed from them. It goes on, “He has allotted our fields to traitors.”

The answer is False. Micah 2:5 says, “Therefore, you will have no one in the assembly of the LORD to divide the land by lot.” Dividing land by lot is how shares were handed out. These people won't have anyone standing up there for them.

The answer is that disgrace will not overtake them. Here is what the preachers say: “Do not preach these things; disgrace will not overtake us.” They're sure disgrace won't overtake them. I bet that's a lot of confidence to pack into one sentence, friends.
The answer is False. The LORD asks, “Do not My words bring good to him who walks uprightly?” The one the verse names is the person who walks uprightly, friends. Power isn't mentioned there.

The answer is an enemy. The LORD says, “But of late My people have risen up like an enemy…” These are His own people, and they're acting like an enemy toward each other. That's a hard thing to hear, friends.

The answer is their splendid robes. The LORD says, “You strip off the splendid robe from unsuspecting passersby like men returning from battle.” The passersby weren't expecting a thing. They're just walking along, and somebody takes their robe.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “You drive the women of My people from their pleasant homes.” These are His people, and the homes are pleasant ones. I think this part is heavy, friends, so it's okay to just sit with it a second.

The answer is that this is not their place of rest. The LORD says, “Arise and depart, for this is not your place of rest…” The land they've been grabbing isn't a resting place for them. They won't settle in and relax there, friends.

The answer is that he'd be just the preacher for them. Micah says it with a bit of a sting: “he would be just the preacher for this people!” This is about a man of wind who falsely says he will preach of wine and strong drink. I think that's the sharpest line in the chapter, friends.

The answer is sheep. The LORD says, “I will bring them together like sheep in a pen, like a flock in the midst of its pasture…” After all the hard words, this is a gathering. He says He will “surely gather” them and collect the remnant of Israel.
The answer is False. The verse ends with “…a noisy throng.” A whole flock packed in together is not a hushed room, friends. The LORD gathers them anyway, noise and all.

The answer is gate. Micah 2:13 says, “One who breaks open the way will go up before them; they will break through the gate, and go out by it.” Somebody goes ahead and opens the way, and they follow through. They don't have to push through alone, friends.

The answer is their King the LORD. Micah 2:13 says, “Their King will pass through before them, the LORD as their leader.” He goes first, and the flock follows. The remnant doesn't have to find the way out on its own, friends.
